sections.h2: A fast-growing city and what it means for a sale
sections.html:
Clermont had 28,742 residents in 2010, 43,021 in 2020 and 52,812 in the July 2025 estimate, putting growth at 22.8% above the 2020 base in just over five years. The typical owner-occupied house carried a value of $418,400 across 2020 through 2024, and 68.1% of housing units are occupied by their owners.

Newer neighborhoods change a seller's checklist. Roof, plumbing and permit records tend to be fresh on a recent build, while a house with unpermitted work needs to be sorted out before closing.

sections.h2: Is your mailing address inside Clermont city limits?
sections.html:
Not always. A Clermont mailing address does not prove a parcel lies within city limits. The city tells owners to search the address on the Lake County Property Appraiser site, open the Alternate Key and read the millage group. A plain number marks unincorporated Lake County, and letters such as GR or MI mark Groveland or Minneola.

The answer decides which building department issued your permits, which codes applied and which tax bill you will split at closing. Confirm it first, then request permit records from the right office.

The city's Building Services FAQ says almost everything may need a permit, with exceptions such as replacing kitchen cabinets, flooring and painting. A homeowner can pull their own permit only for a residence they own and occupy, and they sign an owner-builder affidavit. The city also warns that a contractor who asks you to pull the permit yourself may be a red flag.

Buyers and their inspectors compare visible work to the record. A few items from the FAQ:

  • Fences need a permit, including repair and replacement. Height cannot exceed 6 feet behind the building line or 4 feet in front of it.
  • Tree removal needs a permit costing $25 regardless of how many trees, with a site plan of canopy, understory and palm trees.
  • A permit stays active only with one approved inspection every six months.

If you hold a stalled permit, ask Building Services how to close it before listing.

The city draws a firm line. Your responsibility for water begins where the line meets the city-owned water meter, and for sewer it begins where your lateral joins the city main in the street. A leak or blockage on your side is your cost, and one on the city's side is the city's.

Homes with water pressure of 80 psi or more need a pressure-reducing valve under building codes, and the homeowner owns and maintains it. A failing valve or lateral turns up in inspections, so test yours before you list.

sections.h2: Florida deed tax and your tax bill
sections.html:
Lake County deeds bear the state's tax at 70 cents on each $100 of price. Whoever signs can be held liable, and the clerk collects when the deed is recorded. Your closing agent can show the figure before you agree on a price.

Value is set on January 1, exemption applications are due March 1, and a November payment earns 4 percent off. Once the house sells, the homestead value resets to full just value the next January 1. That means a buyer's first bill may be higher than yours, which is worth mentioning to anyone comparing tax records.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Clermont rental with a tenant inside?
sections.html:
Yes, and the lease usually decides what happens next. Notice periods vary with the tenancy: at least 30 days before a monthly period ends, 60 days for year-to-year and 7 days for week-to-week. For unpaid rent, the written notice is 3 days, excluding weekends and court holidays.

Read the lease for an end date, deposit terms and any right of entry for showings. Some cash buyers will take a rented house with the lease running, so rent keeps arriving.

Foreclosures here run through the courts. Once final judgment is entered, the clerk schedules a public auction within 20 to 35 days, and the high bidder posts 5 percent. Leftover funds go to whoever claims them before the clerk reports them as unclaimed.

Lenders who want the faster order-to-show-cause route meet an obstacle on owner-occupied homes, because a homestead exemption on the latest tax roll creates a presumption that the owner lives there. If you sell before the auction, the payoff comes from the proceeds and equity may be left for you. Questions about timing belong with a Florida attorney or your servicer.

sections.h2: How does probate affect an inherited Clermont home?
sections.html:
An heir cannot sell until a court gives someone authority, normally a personal representative. Summary administration, a lighter court process, can apply to a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less, or to one where the owner died over two years back. A representative's deed under a probated will is among those that owe no deed tax.

Creditors have until three months after the first published notice, or 30 days after a known creditor is served, whichever ends last. Florida collects no estate tax for deaths after 2004. Agree on dates with the probate clerk and a title company before accepting an offer.

When several buyers respond, line up their offers side by side. Look past the headline price to the closing date, any contingencies and who covers which costs. Schedule showings in blocks so your household is not disrupted all week, and keep valuables out of sight. On closing day, bring photo ID, your keys and garage remotes, and confirm in advance how and when your proceeds will arrive. Afterward, hold on to the final settlement statement and a copy of the recorded deed for your tax records.

sections.h2: Preparing paperwork for a quick close
sections.html: Gather the deed, recent tax bills, lender payoff letters, permit records and any lease before you take calls from buyers. Have each buyer write down the price, closing date and the split of costs. An aging roof or unpermitted work should be disclosed early. A cash buyer can accept the property as-is and price the problem in. Before signing day, review the draft settlement statement with your title agent and ask about any line that is unclear.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Clermont house sell for cash?
faqs.a: Often within a few weeks, because a cash buyer skips underwriting and the appraisal. Title work and liens can still set the pace. Get the offer and the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Must a Clermont seller show a permit history?
faqs.a: A permit history is not required to list, but open permits can delay closing. Call Clermont Building Services to learn whether any permit at your address is unfinished and what inspections are needed.

faqs.q: What if my Clermont house has an old roof or unpermitted work?
faqs.a: An as-is sale is allowed, and cash buyers take houses that way. Disclose what you know, and expect a buyer to price in the repair or permit cleanup.

faqs.q: Who pays the Lake County deed tax?
faqs.a: Most contracts assign it to the seller, but the state can collect from any signer. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, so put the allocation in writing.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption survive a sale?
faqs.a: It ends with the sale. The buyer applies by March 1 for their own, and the parcel goes back to just value the following January 1.
